sections.overview: MacConnell’s Bat is a neotropical leaf-nosed bat in the family Phyllostomidae.
sections.identification: It is a small, pale bat with bright yellow ears and noseleaf in life; these features help distinguish it from other leaf-nosed bats.
sections.habitat: It occurs in tropical Central and northern South America, including Amazonian forests, where it roosts in foliage and in leaf tents.
sections.diet: A Peruvian community study classified it as a strict frugivore; the small sample of documented fruits does not establish a complete menu.
sections.behavior: It uses foliage shelters, including small tents formed by modified palm leaves.
sections.reproduction: Field records in Peru include pregnant females in September, while older regional accounts report breeding in both dry and rainy seasons; timing may vary geographically.
sections.ecology: Its taxonomic history includes placements in Ectophylla and Vampyressa, while current mammal databases retain Mesophylla as its genus.
sections.conservation: The Mammal Diversity Database reports a global IUCN category of Least Concern; that broad status does not rule out local habitat pressures.
